commit.message: Note in the design that the log keeps the client's put encoding

files.patch:
@@ -133,7 +133,7 @@ The WAL crash test runs 500 seeds of random appends, suffix replacements and cra
 
 **Committer.** `internal/core` is one node's committer as an event and effect machine. Its inputs are method calls: `Submit` (a client request), `Step` (a Raft message from a peer), `Tick` (one clock tick) and `Persisted` (a disk write finished). `Process` runs Raft until it has nothing left to do and returns `Effects`: persist jobs, messages to send and replies. The driver calls these from one goroutine and carries out the effects. In the real node that driver is the committer goroutine; in the simulator it is the event loop.
 
-- **Writes.** `Submit` validates the request with `mvcc.Check*` and then, like etcd, limits the size of the marshaled `InternalRaftRequest` that wraps a write to 1.5 MiB. Its header holds a request ID; the core sizes it with a 10-byte varint ID. That is etcd v3.7.2's strictest case (a member ID with bit 15 set, as in the difftest), which this matches to the byte (#62); for other member IDs etcd accepts one or more bytes more. Reads do not go through Raft and have only gRPC's limit. Then it queues the write. `Process` packs every queued write into one Raft entry, so the batch holds whatever arrived since the last call. The byte cap is `MaxBatchBytes` (4 MiB), and there is no timer. Each write in the entry carries its origin node, the origin's boot ID and the request ID (`core/codec.go`). A Put from a client stays in its wire form from the socket to the entry: the connection reader checks it with `core.ParsePut`, `Submit` validates and sizes it from its fields, and `Process` copies the client's bytes into the entry, the one encode of the batch. Its reply is the revision, term and previous key, which the connection writer encodes as a PutResponse without building a protobuf message. Raft is `RawNode` with `AsyncStorageWrites`, so the local append comes out as a `PersistJob`. The driver appends every queued job to the WAL, syncs once and reports each job with `Persisted`. The core then appends the entries to its in-memory Raft log and steps the responses. When an entry commits, the core applies it to the index on the spot and answers the requests whose origin and boot match its own. A boot ID is random per process start, so an entry proposed before a restart never answers a request made after it. Within one boot, the driver never reuses a request ID, because a write that timed out can still commit later. A write that the index rejects at apply time (an unknown lease, a missing key for `ignore_value`, a range at a compacted or future revision) is answered with etcd's error on every replica and changes nothing.

The byte cap is `MaxBatchBytes` (4 MiB), and there is no timer. Each write in the entry carries its origin node, the origin's boot ID and the request ID (`core/codec.go`). The entry keeps the client's encoding, so a put that repeats a field logs more bytes than etcd's re-encoding would, up to the 2 MiB receive limit; the size limit counts the decoded put. Its reply is the revision, term and previous key, which the connection writer encodes as a PutResponse without building a protobuf message. The core then appends the entries to its in-memory Raft log and steps the responses. When an entry commits, the core applies it to the index on the spot and answers the requests whose origin and boot match its own. Within one boot, the driver never reuses a request ID, because a write that timed out can still commit later.  - **Reads.** Linearizable reads and read-only transactions queue up, and each `Process` turns the queue into one `ReadIndex` request. The reads run against the index once the applied index reaches the read index. Raft drops a `ReadIndex` without a word when a follower knows no leader, when a message is lost, and on every term change. So a batch without an index asks again every 3 ticks and at once when a new leader appears, and batches are served in any order. Serializable reads run at once against local state. The read context carries the boot ID too.
 - **Timeouts.** Every request has a deadline in ticks (`RequestTicks`, 7 s). After it, the request fails with etcd's "request timed out", which is ambiguous: it may still commit. A proposal that Raft drops because there is no leader fails at once with "no leader".
 - **Membership is fixed.** The Raft storage wrapper reports the 3 voters as its configuration, and there are no configuration entries. On start, the core loads the recovered log into memory and Raft applies it again from index 1, which rebuilds the index. That is the whole of recovery until checkpoints exist.
